          lat_pulldown 3x8..10 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds

          dumbbell_press 2x10..12 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          face_pull 2x12..15 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          bicep_curl 2x10..12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          shoulder_stretch 2m
          tricep_stretch 2m

      DAY Friday training 45m "Lower B":
        warmup:
          walking 5m
        main straight_sets:
          trap_bar_deadlift 3x5..6 rpe 6 rest 150 seconds
          hip_thrust 3x8..10 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds
          leg_extension 2x12..15 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          hip_adduction 2x12..15 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          seated_calf_raise 2x12..15 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          butterfly_stretch 2m
          child_pose 2m

I don't have last week's per-session breakdown. I only have the summary: 18 working sets per session, 4 weeks of high-volume hypertrophy, RPE 8.5 on compounds. If you send the actual session logs, I can set the deload targets from them.

Until then, here's a working basis:

- **Typical deload volume:** about 40-60% of the prior block, so roughly **9-11 working sets per session**.
- **My draft is heavier than that.** It runs 12-14 sets per session, a cut of only about 25-35% from 18. If you want a true deload, I'd bring it down to around 9-11 sets, spread across the same exercises, at RPE 6.

If you confirm the target, I'll rebuild the week at that volume. If you send the logs, I'll base it on his actual per-session numbers instead.

Test submaximally, log the data, and keep fatigue low. Don't do true max attempts this week.

**Good options:**

- **Repeat-load tracking.** Use the same weights he used in the last block on the main lifts (squat, deadlift, row, overhead press). Record reps and RPE at those loads. A drop in RPE at the same load shows strength gains even without a max effort.
- **Submax e-1RM estimates.** On squat and trap bar deadlift, work up to a load he can do for 3 reps at RPE 7 (about 2-3 reps in reserve), then estimate 1RM with a standard calculator. Keep it to one work set after warm-ups.
- **Bodyweight and reps-to-failure checks.** Pull-ups, dips, or push-ups for max reps at RPE 8 or below. These show upper-body strength without a heavy bench test, which suits his shoulder.
- **Plank or hollow hold time.** Simple, low-fatigue, and a good trunk marker.
- **Grip or carry.** A farmer's walk for distance at a moderate load, or a dead hang for time.

**Avoid this week:**

- Any true 1RM or 3RM on bench, squat, or deadlift
- Anything that drives reps to true failure
- Bench-specific testing, given the shoulder

**Where to test:** Put the tests at the end of Monday's and Friday's sessions, or on the Wednesday mobility day as a short add-on. Keep them away from the hardest compound work.

If you want, I can add these tests into the week's DSL as a dedicated testing block.
